concept: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

claims.text: MongoDB documents this inclusive M30–M60 General-class boundary: forbid(principal, action == ResourcePolicy::Action::"cluster.modify", resource) when { (context.cluster has minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue && context.cluster.minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue < 30) || (context.cluster has maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue && context.cluster.maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue > 60) }; (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Use /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources to detect existing violations and remediate them; applying a policy does not automatically rewrite pre-existing configurations. The independent Foojay walkthrough demonstrates unchanged but flagged resources. (high confidence)

Guard optional attributes before comparing them. Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation; MongoDB’s tier example uses has checks. Whether Atlas adds stricter runtime error handling is not established here. (medium confidence)

The minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue and maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue attributes represent the current tier or the minimum and maximum autoscaling sizes; author against these bounds rather than checking only a desired current tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation. Issue #2428 illustrates incorrect string membership using in, corrected with set.contains(value), and maintainers identify it as invalid unvalidated policy rather than an engine bug. This is a general authoring caution, not evidence of an Atlas exploit. (high confidence)

A practitioner walkthrough reports successful Terraform deployment and blocked noncompliant requests, but does not demonstrate enforcement of a tier or autoscaling cap. Treat its cap discussion as guidance rather than an independent cap test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-13)

Atlas Resource Policies add organization-wide configuration guardrails to RBAC; project exceptions allow narrower application. Cluster tier caps are a documented cost-control use. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

MongoDB explicitly excludes Low CPU and NVMe SSD classes from its sample General class tier restriction; do not describe that sample as a universal instance-size cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Atlas accepts forbid policies, excludes permit statements, and allows role-authorized operations by default. Generic Cedar instead defaults to denial without a matching permit; do not transfer its default directly to Atlas. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Existing autoscaling bounds can exceed a newly introduced policy and continue scaling beyond it, although manual scaling beyond the policy is blocked. Inspect /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources and reconcile existing bounds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Manage resource policies as code with the MongoDB Atlas Terraform provider; an independently authored Foojay walkthrough embeds Cedar bodies in mongodbatlas_resource_policy, while the organization module supports applying policies to existing organizations. (high confidence)

Upper and lower cluster tier constraints were publicly announced on March 3, 2025 for provisioning, scaling and updates; this dated preview announcement is historical evidence, not a statement of current preview status. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-03)
The min/max General-class context values cover the current tier and autoscaling bounds. The example does not constrain Low CPU or NVMe SSD clusters. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

Terraform can carry Cedar in mongodbatlas_resource_policy policies[].body, with org_id and name. Versioning policies alongside infrastructure enables reviewable, repeatable governance changes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)
